front_end_yields.note: Two-year fell 3-4bp after softer core PCE.

long_end_yields.note: 30-year at 5.56%, highest since 2002; eased slightly after PCE.

yield_curve.note: Front end fell more than long end after PCE.

dollar.note: Best month since June; stronger dollar weighs on gold.

oil.note: Brent ~$103, up 0.6%; diesel at record, flows costly.

gold.note: Down 5-6% on month, worst since June; still above $4,000.

credit_spreads.note: HY spreads wider six sessions, +40-50bp; widest since March.

equity_futures.note: S&P futures little changed; Nasdaq slightly lower.

fed.market_pricing: October hike odds near 50%; December hike still priced, one more late-year hike.

earnings_ai.note: AI capex/OpenAI funding strong; IPO delays and regulatory pushback temper.

geopolitics.note: Middle East war, Hormuz blockade, Russia diesel ban; broader conflict concerns.

consumer.note: Confidence weak, housing frozen; spending and ADP jobs still okay.

brief.summary: Equities were little changed, with S&P futures slightly higher and Nasdaq softer. Long-end Treasury yields remain near multi-decade highs, though soft core PCE pulled front-end yields down 3-4bp and steepened the curve slightly. The dollar had its best month since June, oil stayed elevated near $103 Brent, gold fell 5-6% on the month, and high-yield spreads widened for six sessions. The Fed remains hawkish, with Williams signaling one more hike late this year and October odds near 50%. The dominant narrative is an energy-driven inflation shock plus heavy Treasury supply, offset by resilient AI-led earnings; tone is cautious and mildly risk-off.
notable_quotes: We are in a high-yield bond world, and no one wants anything to do with it.
